summary: M0 model-only verdict: BENIGN @ 0.80. All sign-ins come from one device (dev-ng-01) and one city (Manisa, TR) across ~two months with a stable, repeated pattern: daytime successes from the university ASN (AS-AEGEAN-EDU, no MFA) and evening MFA-approved logins from a home ISP (TTNET, MFA prompt count = 1). MFA is genuinely prompted and approved each evening, so the person in possession of the device/phone is authenticating — no new device, no impossible travel, no MFA fatigue/bypass, no password change, no external forwarding, and no sent-mail anomalies. The inbox rule only moves mail to an internal Archive-2026 folder via OWA (no external forwarding). The phish_suspect delivery (look-alike domain aegean-edu.com.tr, IBAN/salary lure) is a received, flagged phish with no evidence the user entered credentials or that the account was misused. Suspicious signals are explained by normal remote-evening access by the legitimate user, so there is no confirmed account takeover and no exposure requiring human escalation.
limitations: M0 ablation: Nemotron alone, no tools, no Critic, no Risk Gate, no DQ. Not a product configuration.
